1) blastomere behaviour in human embryos is diagnostic of embryo ploidy by day three; and 2) chromosome-containing fragments and micronuclei are frequently observed in aneuploid human embryos and may persist or reabsorb during interphase.
blastomere cell cycle timing and fragmentation behaviour are diagnostic of ploidity in four-cell human blastocysts, with implications for clinical practice in reducing transfer of aneuploids.
blastomere cell cycle timing and fragmentation are diagnostic of ploidity in human four-cell embryos.

the development of a novel non-invasive approach to identify aneuploid blastomeres at the four-cell stage in human embryos.
the development of non-invasive methods that can identify embryos that are more likely to implant and lead to live birth.
the identification of novel markers of human embryo ploidy that may improve the efficiency of IVF treatment.

blastomere cell-cycle parameters are diagnostic of ploidity in human embryos.

blastomere dynamics can be used as a non-invasive method to detect aneuploids and to identify those embryos with a higher likelihood of miscarriage.
